findings: Normal axis with early repolarisation change

echoTasks.find: Calcified cusps with reduced but present systolic opening on two dimensional imaging
High velocity systolic jet with a late peaking envelope on continuous wave Doppler from the apical window
Thickened cusps with restricted systolic opening in short axis

exam.general: Comfortable older woman, no distress, mild hypertension on record
exam.other: Carotids brisk, no delay, lungs clear

history.a: Exertional breathlessness for 4 months on climbing to the second floor, no chest pain or fainting
Hypertensive for 8 years on amlodipine, sugars borderline
Detected murmur at a camp echo a year ago, advised yearly review
Homemaker caring for grandchildren, walks daily

keyPoints: Arrange 6 to 12 monthly echo surveillance with symptom review, per the ESC valvular guideline
Treat hypertension to target while watching for symptoms that mark progression
Counsel on prompt reporting of angina, syncope or breathlessness, which would trigger referral
Keep dental hygiene and endocarditis awareness without routine antibiotic prophylaxis
Plan exercise advice that avoids strenuous isometric effort until reassessed
management.model: Structured surveillance with blood pressure control and red flag counselling until intervention criteria appear

stem: A 61 year old homemaker from Kochi with a known murmur presents for yearly review with new exertional breathlessness but no angina or syncope. A grade 3 ejection murmur radiates to the carotids with an ejection sound.
teaching: Moderate means velocity 3 to 4 m per s with area 1.0 to 1.5 sq cm, and symptoms decide the next step
An ejection sound marks a still mobile valve, while its loss marks progression
Surveillance intervals plus red flag counselling are the core resident skill here
Continuity area needs the outflow diameter, the sample volume site, and the highest velocity window
title: Moderate aortic stenosis under surveillance
